concepts.interpretation: Most delay (68% of all waiting, 9528.2 person-s per run) builds behind the South stair S198B exterior door (H1). That door carries 25% of people on only 7% of exit capacity and runs saturated for 110 s, fed mainly by Construction lab 0238, Medium classroom 0230 and the F3 grad studios. The same southern stack also queues upstream: at door D-F2-015 into South stair S298B (H4, H5) and at door D-F3-021 at the end of corridor C399D (H2), while 20.6 people per run are caught by smoke in South stair S198B. A second bottleneck is door D-F1-003 between the Central stair and the Lobby (H3, H6), saturated for 65 s. Meanwhile the East door from storage 0140A and the West entry each sit under-used at about 7-8% of people for 18% of capacity.

regulations: New structure with foundations and openings in the exterior wall on every floor: needs a structural engineer and a building permit.
Exit stair: 48 in clear width (0.3 in per person), handrails both sides, risers at most 7 in, treads at least 11 in (NFPA 101 7.2.2; verify against the adopted code).
An exterior exit stair needs weather protection and separation from openings in the wall beside it, or must be enclosed.

built.title: Direct exit to outside from Central stair S198A (68 in door pair at the foot of the stair)
built.why: A direct exterior door from the Central stair at ground level lets the stair discharge without passing through D-F1-003 into the lobby. (Gives the people queuing at door D-F1-003 (Lobby C199A (F1) / Central stair S198A (F1)) a second way out 10 ft from the queue, instead of waiting for a door that passes at most 0.73 people/s.)

regulations: Wider opening needs a new header; rated walls need a rated double-door assembly.
